text:
maria: FYI I brought up umbrage-compact-int6 in staging and ran our standard recall/cluster sanity. Quick first pass shows a notable drop vs the int8 baseline — mainly in recall@5. holding notes below.

maria: command I ran:
```bash
./eval_embeddings --model umbrage-compact-int6 --holdout holdout_v2 --metrics recall@1,recall@5,ndcg --calib 10000
```

ci-bot: eval job 4821 finished — recall@1: 0.412, recall@5: 0.742, ndcg: 0.591
ci-bot: baseline (umbrage-int8) — recall@1: 0.439, recall@5: 0.804, ndcg: 0.623

sam: that's ~6.2% absolute drop at R@5. any stratification by query length or domain?

maria: initial stratify by query length shows short queries (<8 tokens) take the biggest hit. long queries less affected. Also saw more noisy neighbors in UMAP visualization :eyes:

raj: int6 quant often hurts short-context semantics. what quant config did you use? per-channel or per-tensor? symmetric or asymmetric?

maria: per-channel symmetric with clamp-scale heuristics (the default from our int6 pipeline). calibr set was 10k random examples from prod-ish holdout.

raj: try per-channel asymmetric and increase calib to 100k. also probe per-layer outlier clamps — sometimes top-k activation tails cause topk mismatch in similarity.

maria: good call. I'll kick that off.

olivia: can we also run a quick recall delta by cohort (faq vs conversational vs docs)? helps us know if it's domain-specific.

maria: putting cohorts in the job now.

ci-bot: job 4822 queued (umbrage-compact-int6, calib=100k, quant=per-channel-asym, cohorts enabled)

sam: also try a hybrid fallback experiment: route ~10% of canary traffic to int6 and 90% to int8 but record both embeddings for offline eval. that way we can compare in-prod samples without user facing regressions.

olivia: +1. add a route-level policy to console: canary=10%, record-only for int6 embeddings, serve int8.

raj: small note — check kv-cache compatibility if you change per-layer scaling; embedding vector norms can shift and affect cosine.

maria: noted. I'll add normalized-cosine postprocessing to the eval pipeline to isolate raw vector shifts vs angle changes.

ci-bot: job 4822 started

maria: quick interim result from cohort split (first 5k of calib): FAQ cohort R@5 dropped 0.11 absolute, conversational dropped 0.03, docs dropped 0.07.

sam: that suggests calibration skew — maybe calibration set underrepresents FAQ short queries. run a stratified calibration sample with heavier FAQ weight.

maria: re-running with stratified calib (faq-heavy). command:
```bash
./eval_embeddings --model umbrage-compact-int6 --calib-file calib_faq_heavy_100k.jsonl --quant-config per-channel-asym --metrics recall@1,recall@5 --cohorts faq,conv,docs
```

ci-bot: job 4823 queued

raj: also snapshot top-1 neighbor differences for a random 5k queries. helps triage whether systematic neighbor swaps (id flips) or general score compression.

maria: will dump neighbor diffs to /tmp/umbrage_int6_neighdiffs_5k.jsonl

ci-bot: job 4823 finished — stratified result partial: FAQ R@5 improved from 0.69 -> 0.75 with faq-heavy calib, overall R@5 now 0.778. still below int8 baseline but much closer.

olivia: nice. any visualization for neighbor id flip rate?

maria: early neighbor-diff sampling shows ~12% top1 id flips for short queries, many flips are semantically close but some are noise. sharing notebook link: https://redwood-internal/notebooks/umbrage-int6-neighdiffs

sam: suggests two mitigations: 1) better calibration set (we're doing this), 2) small per-axis correction (scale adjust) post-quant to match int8 norm dist. also consider hybrid ensemble: use int6 for long queries, int8 for short.

raj: agree. ensemble rule could be cheap: length > 12 -> int6 else int8. easy to implement in router.

maria: plan of action:
- pause wide rollout; keep disabled in console
- finish stratified calibration runs (in progress)
- run per-axis scale-correct and re-eval neighbor id flips
- run canary-record (10% recording) so we can gather in-prod deltas without impacting users
- if delta < 1.5% absolute at R@5 and idflip<7% for short queries, we consider canarying serving path

olivia: can you open a follow-up ticket with the eval job ids and attach the notebook? I'll add the console rollout hold flag.

maria: creating ticket ML-1127 with job ids [4821,4822,4823] and the notebook link.

ci-bot: created ticket ML-1127 assigned to maria

sam: thanks — ping me when the 10% record canary data lands, I'll run the paired-sample significance test.

maria: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:

raj: appreciate the quick triage, good catch on the short-query sensitivity :eyes:

olivia: :rocket: keep us posted
